title: Window and Door Rebates in Coquitlam 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: Coquitlam homes can claim $100 per window or door from BC Hydro. 16,535 households live in pre-1981 homes. Rules, a worked example and how to claim.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Coquitlam
lead: Coquitlam's hillside neighbourhoods have a lot of large windows, which are expensive to replace. The cap of $2,000 pays for 20 openings, so a house with many big windows will hit it.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Coquitlam
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Coquitlam hillside house

A house with 16 windows and 4 doors reaches the 20-opening cap. The rebate is $2,000, no matter whether the windows cost $20,000 or $40,000. Rebates cannot exceed the invoice cost, but at these prices the cap is the limit.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 55,945 households in Coquitlam. About 16,535 (30%) live in homes built before 1981, and 7,305 are owner-occupied detached houses from that period. Another 36% of households live in apartments and 31% rent. About 69% of households own their home.
Coquitlam's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.7°C and the coldest day was -16.8°C. Winters are damp and mild. Comfort and condensation are the main gains, with a modest effect on the bill.

The rebate is $100 per opening, not per square foot, so a big picture window earns the same as a small one. That makes the rebate cover more of the cost on small windows and less on large ones. If you are replacing only a few large windows, ask whether the quote leaves room under the cap for doors too.

Each rough opening is one opening. A bay window with several sections is one. Eligible windows must carry a listing from CSA, Intertek, Labtest, QAI or NFRC and have a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower. Skylights are not eligible, and windows must replace existing ones.

BC Hydro pays a bonus of up to $2,000 when you finish more than one eligible upgrade, but its page does not give a formula, so ask when you apply. FortisBC lists a $300 second-upgrade bonus or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000. Windows pair naturally with insulation, since both cut heat loss through the building envelope.

BC Hydro publishes a consumer guide for window and door replacement. It covers frame materials, glazing types and what to ask a contractor. Read it before you take quotes, so you can compare units on the same terms. The program only checks the U-factor, certification and installation rules, so the other choices are yours.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Confirm the home is electric-heated and at least 12 months old.
Get quotes that list each window and door with its U-factor and certification.
Photograph the label on each unit.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: Does a larger window earn more?
No. The rebate is $100 per opening regardless of size.
How many openings reach the cap?
Do I need a U-factor of 1.22?
Yes. It must be 1.22 W/m2-K or lower.
Not under this program. BC Hydro has a separate program for condos.
